prerequisites: Foundations of mechanical design treated in Machine Technology I (especially stress calculation, static failure criteria, and fatigue diagrams)

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the fundamental criteria of mechanical design established in Machine Technology I to rigid or elastic joint elements and different types of transmissions.
Complete the specialized study of mechanical components and machine elements, ensuring the ability to approach calculation and design problems of mechanical assemblies.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of machine technology.

syllabus_topics: Hobbing of involute profile gear wheels
Calculation for surface pressure of cylindrical gears
Calculation for bending of cylindrical gears
General aspects of conical gear calculation
Calculation for surface pressure of conical gears
Calculation for bending of conical gears
teaching_methods: Study of didactic material (base text chapters)
Discussion and resolution of doubts (teacher-student and student-student interaction)
Distance practicals (design and analysis of a mechanical assembly using Autodesk Inventor)
Use of the virtual course via AGORA portal
Submission of documents through virtual course links
assessment_rules: The exam consists of solving two problems, each contributing 50% to the exam score. To pass the exam, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required. Passing the exam is an indispensable condition to pass the course, as is passing the distance practicals. Voluntary Continuous Assessment Tests (PECs) can improve the final grade by up to 15% if the exam score is 5 or higher. The final grade is the exam score if it is below 5; if the exam is passed but practicals are not, the final grade is 4.9 (fail); if both are passed, the final grade is calculated as NF = (1 + CPED x CPV) x NEX, where NEX is the exam score, CPED is the sum of PEC coefficients (max 0.15), and CPV is the virtual practicals coefficient (between 0.8 and 1.2), with CPED x CPV not exceeding 0.15.
